- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts too high; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.3) mid-period, model frequently fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for 2–4 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecasted maxima.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., ±0.2), model shows mean-reversion bias; forecast should be closer to recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of true peak.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period corrections; add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment turns negative in last 3–5 days.
